description: Fire's vetted font catalogue: the families a type set spec (the theme record's `type` object) may name. Every family is open-licensed, has a Latin woff2 subset that `node scripts/fonts.mjs add <family>` can copy or download, and carries measured metrics and the metric-matched fallback that keeps the layout still while it loads. fire/js/fonts.js is generated from this file by scripts/build-typefaces.mjs; scripts/test/fonts.test.mjs holds the two together.
measuredBy: @capsizecss/metrics 4.5.0 (the font files' own tables: units per em, hhea ascent/descent/line gap, OS/2 x-height and cap height, and xWidthAvg, the Latin letters' advance widths weighted by English letter frequency). One family, Big Shoulders Display, is not in that package; it was measured with fontkit 3.0.0 from the same woff2 file with the same weighting (marked on the family).

voices.neutral: Plain and even; disappears into the interface.
voices.technical: Precise, a little engineered; at home with code and data.
voices.editorial: Reads like print: contrast, character, a point of view.
voices.playful: Quirks and personality; not for a bank.
voices.condensed: Narrow letters; many characters per line, strong at display sizes.
voices.wide: Extended letters; takes space, reads a size larger.
voices.geometric: Built from circles and straight lines.
voices.humanist: Calligraphic stroke contrast; easy over long text.
voices.loud: Built to be seen: heavy, extreme or unmissable.

stacks.sans: system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Roboto, "Helvetica Neue", Arial, sans-serif
stacks.serif: ui-serif, "Iowan Old Style", "Palatino Linotype", Georgia, serif

fallbackAgainst.note: A fallback face is a local() system font with the metric overrides that make it occupy the same space as the web font (size-adjust from the average letter width; ascent, descent and line-gap overrides from the vertical metrics). local() cannot name system-ui or ui-monospace, so the reference is the font those stacks resolve to most often and that is on every desktop: Arial, Times New Roman, Courier New. The family's stack (sans, serif or mono) picks the reference; the CSS stack still ends in system-ui or ui-monospace.
